content.title: About
content.content: Bread is a baked product made from dough of flour, water, yeast and salt. Cheese is a dairy product obtained by curdling milk and allowing it to mature. Together they are commonly enjoyed as sandwiches, snacks and various dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bread is one of the oldest foods, with a history dating back over 14,000 years.
There are more than 2,000 varieties of cheese, differing in flavor, texture and aging process.
In many cultures bread symbolizes hospitality and prosperity.
Certain cheeses contain probiotics that support gut health.
The bread‑cheese combination appears in traditional dishes worldwide, such as French croque‑monsieur or Italian panini.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Bread provides quick‑release carbohydrates, while cheese supplies protein and fat, making a balanced energy boost.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Cheese is a rich source of calcium for bone health, and many cheeses are fortified with vitamin D.

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: Live‑culture cheeses (e.g., brie, camembert) help maintain a healthy intestinal microbiome.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole‑grain bread contains B1, B3 and folate, essential for metabolism.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Cheese delivers complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to casein or lactose found in cheese.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Many cheeses are salty, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Gluten in bread
items.content: Traditional bread contains gluten, unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The bread‑cheese combo can be calorie‑rich, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Some cheeses are high in saturated fat, which may affect cholesterol levels.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread soft cheese on bread, make sandwiches, toast with melted cheese, or serve cheese slices alongside fresh bread. Cheese can be grated, cubed, added to salads, casseroles, or enjoyed as a snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bread in a dry place in a bread box or bag; freeze if not used quickly. Keep cheese refrigerated, wrapped in parchment and foil to prevent drying; hard cheeses last weeks, soft cheeses a few days.
